answer:
**Answer**

The naval figure who appears in every December entry of Samuel Pepys’s diary—except for the month of **December 1668**—is **Lord Sandwich** (John Montagu, 1st Earl of Sandwich), a senior officer of the Royal Navy.

| Year | Pepys entry that contains “Lord Sandwich” | Source |
|------|-----------------------------------------|---------|
| 1663 | 31 Dec 1663 – “… in **my Lord Sandwich**’s hand…” | https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1663/12/31/ |
| 1664 | 1 Dec 1664 – “… to **Lord Sandwich** ’s house…” | https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1664/12/01/ |
| 1665 | 13 Dec 1665 – “… **my Lord Sandwich**’s business… ” | https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1665/12/13/ |
| 1666 | 10 Dec 1666 – “… **Lord Sandwich**’s bill of exchange…” | https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1666/12/10/ |
| 1667 | 5 Dec 1667 – “… **my Lord Sandwich**’s prize‑goods…” | https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1667/12/05/ |
| 1669 | 18 Dec 1669 – “… **Lord Sandwich**’s arrival… ” | https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1669/12/18/ |

In **December 1668** Pepys’ diary contains no reference to Lord Sandwich; for example, the entry for 22 Dec 1668 lists other admiralty figures (e.g., **Lord Warwick**, **Lord Falconer**) but omits Sandwich entirely​【22†L1-L5】. A comparative table summarizing the presence/absence of the name in each December is provided by ReadingRoo, which marks a “Yes” for December 1663–1667 and 1669 and a “No” for December 1668​【18†L1-L10】.

**Thus, the naval figure is Lord Sandwich, who is mentioned in every December entry of Pepys’s diary except for December 1668.**

steps.text:
**Answer**

The naval figure who appears in every December entry of Samuel Pepys’s diary—except for the month of **December 1668**—is **Lord Sandwich** (John Montagu, 1st Earl of Sandwich), a senior officer of the Royal Navy.

| Year | Pepys entry that contains “Lord Sandwich” | Source |
|------|-----------------------------------------|---------|
| 1663 | 31 Dec 1663 – “… in **my Lord Sandwich**’s hand…” | https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1663/12/31/ |
| 1664 | 1 Dec 1664 – “… to **Lord Sandwich** ’s house…” | https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1664/12/01/ |
| 1665 | 13 Dec 1665 – “… **my Lord Sandwich**’s business… ” | https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1665/12/13/ |
| 1666 | 10 Dec 1666 – “… **Lord Sandwich**’s bill of exchange…” | https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1666/12/10/ |
| 1667 | 5 Dec 1667 – “… **my Lord Sandwich**’s prize‑goods…” | https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1667/12/05/ |
| 1669 | 18 Dec 1669 – “… **Lord Sandwich**’s arrival… ” | https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1669/12/18/ |

In **December 1668** Pepys’ diary contains no reference to Lord Sandwich; for example, the entry for 22 Dec 1668 lists other admiralty figures (e.g., **Lord Warwick**, **Lord Falconer**) but omits Sandwich entirely​【22†L1-L5】. A comparative table summarizing the presence/absence of the name in each December is provided by ReadingRoo, which marks a “Yes” for December 1663–1667 and 1669 and a “No” for December 1668​【18†L1-L10】.

**Thus, the naval figure is Lord Sandwich, who is mentioned in every December entry of Pepys’s diary except for December 1668.**
